source: Minchat Shai on Gen 13:7 (quoting the Ramah; against the Zohar's homily)
claim_en: THE QUARREL-WORD SPELLING LAW (the Ramah): riv ('quarrel/dispute') is written PLENE (with yod) everywhere in the Torah except ONE — 'do not answer in a dispute' (Exod 23:2), the Masorah's own mnemonic. SNAPSHOT, the lemma's whole Torah career (ten tokens, bare and inflected): every form carries the yod — 13:7 (the herdsmen), Exod 17:7 (Meribah's naming), Exod 23:3/6, Deut 1:12, 17:8, 19:17, 21:5, 25:1 — except exactly Exod 23:2, defective. The Zohar's defective reading HERE is named and declined by all the books.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 13:3 (the books, the Hilleli, the Ramah, the Meiri — against the Zohar)
claim_en: le-masaav ('by his JOURNEYS,' plural) written PLENE with yod — the Zohar's homily reads it defective-singular ('his journey'), but all books new and old, the Hilleli, the Ramah and the Meiri read the yod. SNAPSHOT: the yod stands — the return retraces STAGES, plural.

haya ('had been' — the tent 'where his tent HAD BEEN at the beginning') read MIL'EL (stress retracted), 'the qadma on the HE' in manuscripts and most printings. SNAPSHOT: the accent sits on the first syllable exactly.
na ('please') in al-na tehi carries QADMA (the forward accent-stroke) on the nun — NOT a pausal accent (Minchat Shai's parallels: the smoking oven of 15:17, the morsel of bread of 18:5).

...and THEREFORE the tav of tehi ('let there be') is SOFT (no dagesh, the doubling dot): because the plea-particle's accent does not pause, the next word begins soft. The rule crowns the machine's own device — the corpus's first human LET-NOT (al-na tehi merivah, 'let there be no strife, please') carries its softness in the letter.
THE SEAM ACROSTIC, part 1: the final letters of va-yipardu ish me-al achiv ('and they separated, each from his brother') spell ושלו — the first four letters of ve-shalom ('and peace').

THE SEAM ACROSTIC, part 2: the very next word — אברם ('Abram'), opening 13:12 across the verse-break — supplies the closing mem: ושלום ('and PEACE') spelled by the separation's own finals PLUS the parted man's name. 'To make peace they separated' — and the hint runs to his children: 'do not besiege Moab' (Deut 2:9 — Lot's line spared; edge).

avram VERSE-INITIAL — exactly ONCE in the Torah (13:12, the settling after the parting); the Masorah's pair is 'Abram — HE IS Abraham' (I Chr 1:27; edge): 'in his righteousness from beginning to end — and so Abram SAT, to part from wicked Lot.'

ve-anshei ('and the men of') VERSE-INITIAL — in the Torah exactly twice: the men of SODOM (13:13) and the men of HOLINESS (Exod 22:30, 'men of holiness shall you be to Me') — the Kitzur reads the contrast through torn flesh and hospitality; the third member (Ezek 39:14) rides as an edge.

ve-chataim ('and sinners') — exactly ONE Torah token (13:13); the Masorah's four run a repentance ARC through the Writings: 'transgressors and sinners broken together' (Isa 1:28), 'sinners RETURN to You' (Ps 51:15), 'sinners in the congregation of the righteous' (Ps 1:5) — three edges.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 13:15 (the misleading-verses Masorah)
claim_en: THE THREE VERSES SCRIBES MISQUOTE: u-le-zarakha ad-olam ('and to your seed FOREVER,' 13:15 — the blessing, with LAMED) against u-ve-zarakha ad-olam ('and UPON your seed forever,' Deut 28:46 — the curse-sign, with BET) and Naaman's 'leprosy... to your seed forever' (II Kings 5:27; edge). One letter divides the blessing's forever from the curse's. SNAPSHOT: of the Torah's three bet-form tokens (Jacob's blessing 28:14, Moses' plea Deut 9:29, the curse-sign Deut 28:46), only the CURSE-SIGN runs into 'until forever' — one letter and one step from the blessing's phrase.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 13:15 (context of the trio)
claim_en: ad-olam ('until FOREVER') at its corpus-first (the machine's own find, 13:15): joined by maqqef — forever is one breath with its until.

ve-lo nasa ('and it could not BEAR them') — the pair stands exactly once in the Torah; the Masorah's twin is 'David did not COUNT them' (I Chr 27:23-24; edge): 'they had wealth beyond number.' The land that cannot carry, the census that cannot close.

THE COMPASS-SCAN CONTRAST, arm 1: Abraham's scan OPENS NORTH — tzafonah va-negbah ('northward and southward') adjacent at 13:14 (the Kitzur: shown first the merit of the offerings, slaughtered on the altar's NORTH side).

THE COMPASS-SCAN CONTRAST, arm 2: Jacob's scan (28:14) OPENS AT THE SEA — yamah va-qedmah ('seaward and eastward') adjacent: 'shown that by his merit they would cross the SEA.' The same four points, two openings — each patriarch's scan begins at his own sign.

DISCREPANCY OBSERVATION — gam zarakha ('also your seed,' 13:16): Minchat Shai rules 'WITHOUT maqqef'; SNAPSHOT (Leningrad line) JOINS the two words with maqqef. Filed beside the 12:8 doubled-accent split: accent-writing convention, tradition vs SNAPSHOT; not merged.
va-yavo ('and he came,' 13:18) 'with TEVIR (the broken low accent), not darga (the stair accent)' — SNAPSHOT carries exactly the tevir.

source: Bava Batra 100a:7; Bereshit Rabbah 41:10; Jerusalem Talmud Kiddushin 1:3:5
claim_en: A MODE OF ACQUIRING PROPERTY IS DERIVED FROM OUR 13:17. R. Eliezer holds that WALKING a parcel acquires it, and his stated reason is this verse - 'arise, walk the land in its length and breadth, for to you I will give it'. The Sages dispute the general rule, holding the walking here was love of Abraham, to ease his descendants' conquest. But the Jerusalem Talmud records the AGREED case even on the dissenting view: one who sells another a path, once he has walked it, has acquired it - 'what is the reason? Our verse'. So the verse grounds a live mode of acquisition that all sides accept in at least one case.

check.note: A mode of property acquisition derived from this verse, disputed in scope but agreed in one case even by the dissenters.

claim_en: THE LODGING LAW IS DERIVED TWICE FROM THIS UNIT, AND THE TWO DERIVATIONS DIFFER IN PRACTICE. The rule that a person should not change his lodging is sourced by Rav to our 13:3, 'to the place where his tent had been at the beginning'; R. Yosei ben R. Chanina sources it instead to the same verse's 'on his journeys'. The tradition records a practical difference between the two derivations, on temporary lodging - so the choice of clause inside one verse decides a case.

check.note: Two derivations of one rule from two clauses of the same verse, with a recorded practical difference between them.

claim_en: OUR 13:10 IS RULED TO BE ENTIRELY ABOUT SIN, AND THAT RULING DECIDES A LATER CASE. R. Yosei bar Chanina reads the whole verse as expressions of immorality, matching four of its tokens to later scenes - the raised eyes, the round loaf, the watering, the destruction. R. Yochanan states it flatly at the Babylonian seat: 'this entire verse was stated about sin' - and that premise is then used to decide the question of intent in the discussion of Lot's daughters. The same verse also serves as the PREMISE of a light-and-heavy argument: Egypt is the most praiseworthy of lands by this verse, yet Israel's poorest region outranks its best, so the Land is supreme.

check.note: A verse ruled wholly figurative for sin, that ruling then deciding an intent question elsewhere; and the same verse serving as an a-fortiori premise.

source: Mekhilta DeRabbi Shimon Ben Yochai 21:18; Sifrei Devarim 286:1
claim_en: OUR 13:7's QUARREL IS THE CASE-LAW PARADIGM FOR ASSAULT AND LITIGATION. Two tannaitic seats open their sugyot with it: the injury law's 'when men quarrel' is prefaced 'nothing good comes from quarrel - what caused Lot to separate from that righteous man? Quarrel'; and the lawsuit-opener of the flogging discussion is prefaced the same way. This unit's herdsmen's dispute is the standing illustration at the head of two bodies of law.

check.note: A narrative quarrel used as the opening paradigm of two separate legal discussions.

claim_en: THE TRADITION'S OWN RHETORIC RULE GRADES OUR 13:16 AS LITERAL. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds that Scripture speaks in hyperbole - fortified cities 'to the heavens' - BUT rules that the promises to Abraham, the stars and OUR dust, ARE NOT HYPERBOLE. The corpus thereby marks which of its own numeric similes are to be read as measurements. The dust simile is separately unpacked as four claims - dispersed end to end, blessed only through water, outlasting metal and the nations, trodden - and paired with the stars in a grading rule: when they descend, to the dust; when they rise, to the stars.

check.note: An explicit rule of the tradition marking this verse's simile as literal rather than hyperbolic - a statement about how the corpus's own figures should be read.

source: Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 10:3:4; Sifra, Bechukotai, Section 2 2; Tosefta Shabbat 8:12
claim_en: OUR 13:13 IS SPLIT TEMPORALLY TO DRIVE A RULING, AND ITS VALENCE IS REVERSED AT ONE SEAT. The Mishnah's ruling that the men of Sodom have no share is given its reason from this verse read in two tenses - wicked and sinful IN THIS WORLD, and the added clause FOR THE WORLD TO COME. The Sifra builds its category of deliberate rebellion on the same token, 'to the LORD', which marks one who knows his Master and rebels. Against all of that a Tosefta seat records the opposite valence outright: R. Nehorai holds no city more temperate than Sodom, 'Lot circled all the places and found none as temperate', quoting our 13:12.

check.note: A verse split across two tenses to supply a ruling's reason, with a recorded polarity reversal at another seat.

claim_en: OUR 13:8 IS WEIGHED AS THE SOURCE OF A VERBAL ANALOGY AND DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED. The levirate discussion considers deriving the meaning of brotherhood from this verse's 'for we are brothers' - and rejects it, because here the word means mere kinsmen, preferring a term that is free for the analogy from elsewhere. The unit's own token is examined as a candidate for a formal inference and recorded as declined, with the reason given.

check.note: This unit's token weighed as the base of a verbal analogy and explicitly rejected, the rejection reasoned and recorded.
